Here is the English translation of the given Ancient Greek text from Homer's *Iliad* (Book 9, lines 184–198):

---

Then in turn the lord of men, Agamemnon, answered him:
*"I rejoice, son of Laertes, to hear your words;
for you have spoken all things fairly and in order.
Now I myself wish to swear an oath, and my heart bids me,
nor will I break my swear by the gods. But let Achilles
stay here, even if he is urgent for battle like Ares;
and all the rest of you stay, until the gifts
come from my tent and we establish trustworthy oaths.

But to you I give this command and charge:
Choose the best of the young Achaeans
and bring the gifts from my ship—all that we promised
to give to Achilles yesterday—and lead the women.
And let Talthybius quickly prepare through the wide camp of the Achaeans
a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and Helios."*

---
